advances: Geometric rank of exact sampled exposed-face restrictions under reciprocal integrability. No partition of defect mass or inductive uniform-volume depth claim.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Compatibility identifies the actual hull fiber at $z\in P$ with $K_z$: group the generators of a hull point by base site and apply the compatibility inclusion. There are no other sampled fibers by completeness of $P$. Since $A\ge L\ge0$ on $C$, every positive-coefficient summand of a convex representation of a point of $F$ must have $A=0$. This gives the hull identity and its projection $B=\operatorname{conv}Z_F$. An integer point of $B$ has a lift in $F$ and lies in $P$ by completeness, giving the exact census. In particular $B$ is a lattice polytope, even if the ambient exposed face has larger affine dimension.

The continuous gradient of $A$ cannot be zero: at a nonempty sampled zero fiber it would make the entire $K_z$ zero, contradicting interior positivity of $L$. This rules out $d=0$. For $d\ge1$, a sampled zero fiber cannot have full dimension for the same positivity reason. If it had dimension $d-1$, choose a relative $(d-1)$-ball in that zero face and cone it to an interior point $o$ of $K_z$. Here $A(z,o)>0$. For $0<t<A(z,o)/2$, the cone section at $A=t$ is a translate of the ball dilated by $1-t/A(z,o)\ge1/2$, so its $(d-1)$-measure is bounded below by a positive constant. Orthogonal coordinates along the continuous gradient give the volume factor $dt/|\nabla_x A|$. Thus $\int_{K_z}1/A$ diverges as $\int_0^{A(z,o)/2}dt/t$, whereas $1/A\le1/L$ on the fiber interior. This excludes codimension one, also in $d=1$ where a nonempty zero face would be a point and the cone an interval.

For any nonempty compact convex set $D$ and its linear projection $J$, the fiber at $z\in\operatorname{relint}J$ has dimension $\dim D-\dim J$. To see this, a relative ball around $w_0\in\operatorname{relint}D$ projects onto a relative neighborhood of $z_0=\operatorname{pr}_z w_0$. If $z\ne z_0$, extend the ray from $z_0$ through $z$ a short distance past it inside $J$; choose a lift of that farther point in $D$. Interpolating that lift and the ball gives a relative ball in $D$ at a point above $z$. For $z=z_0$ use the original ball. Intersecting with the affine fiber gives the full vertical kernel of $\operatorname{aff}D$, of dimension $\dim D-\dim J$. In $F$ that kernel lies in the null space of the nonzero continuous gradient of $A$, so its dimension is at most $d-1$. If it equals $d-1$ an interior lattice label of $B$ would give a prohibited $(d-1)$-dimensional sampled fiber. Since every original fiber is $d$-dimensional, $\dim C=\dim\operatorname{conv}P+d$ by taking an affine basis of bases together with one full continuous fiber. Thus a relative facet has the asserted full base dimension and vertical rank $d-1$.

Apply the maximal-minimal-face parity result 347dc8c30a1e79ad to $I=Z_F$: the exact census gives completeness and $\operatorname{conv}I=B$. Every $z\in I$ belongs to an inclusion-maximal minimal face, and the accepted proof gives disjoint relative-interior parity sets of those maximal faces. With an integer origin in $B$, the saturated lattice $\operatorname{lin}(B-B)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ has rank $\dim B$, because $B$ is a lattice polytope. Two points of its affine coset have the same ambient parity exactly when their half-difference belongs to this direction lattice. Thus there are at most $2^{\dim B}$ such classes. Each $E_i$ is cut out in $B$ by a nonnegative affine functional, also allowing the zero functional for $E_i=B$. Pull it back to $F$ to expose $F_i$; its projection is exactly $E_i$. For a sampled $z_i$ in $\operatorname{relint}E_i$, the fiber of $F_i$ over $z_i$ is $F_{z_i}$. The relative-interior fiber formula therefore gives $\dim F_i-\dim E_i=\dim F_{z_i}\le d-2$. The cover follows at every sampled point. A relative facet has no relative-interior integer label in its projection, so all its $E_i$ are proper. If such a label exists then its minimal face is $B$, the only maximal choice.

This cover may overlap, and the dimension calculation concerns the actual affine kernels. It does not identify any defect measure on a piece with uniform Hausdorff measure or prove an unrestricted rate inequality.
statement:
Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, with compatible compact convex $d$-dimensional fibers $K_z$ at every $z\in P$: each Minkowski combination at an integer target in $P$ lies in the target fiber. Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and let $L$ be a finite minimum of affine functions, nonnegative on $C$, positive on each sampled fiber interior, with $\sum_{z\in P}\int_{K_z}L(z,x)^{-1}\,dx<\infty$ (using counting if $d=0$). For an affine majorant $A\ge L$ on $C$, suppose $F=C\cap\{A=0\}$ is nonempty, and put $B=\operatorname{pr}_z F$, $Z_F=\{z\in P:F_z\ne\varnothing\}$.

Then
$$
F=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in Z_F}(\{z\}\times F_z),\qquad
B=\operatorname{conv}Z_F,\qquad Z_F=B\cap\mathbb Z^n.
$$
No such nonempty $F$ exists when $d\le1$. For $d\ge2$, the continuous gradient of $A$ is nonzero, every nonempty sampled $F_z$ has dimension at most $d-2$, and $\dim F-\dim B\le d-1$. Equality in this last bound implies $\operatorname{relint}B\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing$. If $F$ is a relative facet of $C$, then $\dim B=\dim\operatorname{conv}P$ and $\operatorname{relint}B$ is integer-free.

Let $E_1,\ldots,E_h$ be the inclusion-maximal minimal faces of the lattice polytope $B$ at its integer points, allowing $B$ itself. These cover all of $Z_F$ and have nonempty pairwise disjoint relative-interior parity sets in the inherited affine lattice, so $h\le2^{\dim B}$. Each $F_i=F\cap\operatorname{pr}_z^{-1}(E_i)$ is exposed in $F$, projects onto $E_i$, and has vertical affine rank
$$
\dim F_i-\dim E_i\le d-2.
$$
The union of the $F_i$ contains every sampled point of $F$. For a relative facet $F$ each $E_i$ is proper; if $B$ has a relative-interior integer point, the only $E_i$ is $B$ and the rank bound holds on $F$ itself.
title: Reciprocal integrability forces a rank drop on maximal sampled zero-face pieces
